prompts.planning.stages.short: Break this goal into stages: [goal] by [deadline].
prompts.planning.stages.detailed: My goal: [goal]. Deadline: [deadline]. Where I am now: [where I am now]. Break the path into 4–6 stages. For each: a checkable result, a rough timeframe, a concrete first step. Mark the stage where people most often get stuck and how to avoid that.
prompts.planning.stages.refine: Stage [number] is too big. Break it into 1–2 hour tasks.
prompts.planning.stages.check: [time] has passed and I've done [done]. Should I change the plan?
prompts.planning.week.short: Make a weekly plan. My tasks: [tasks]
prompts.planning.week.detailed: Make a weekly plan as a table by day. Fixed commitments: [schedule]. Tasks for the week: [tasks]. Time I can give per day: [hours]. Spread the tasks out, put hard ones when I think best ([morning or evening]), and keep at least one evening free.
prompts.planning.week.refine: Something new has come up on [day] for [time]. Rearrange the plan.
prompts.planning.week.check: The week is over and these weren't done: [not done]. What should carry over and what should be dropped?
prompts.planning.estimate.short: How long will [task] take? Break it down.
prompts.planning.estimate.detailed: Help me estimate the workload: [task]. My experience with this: [experience]. Break it into subtasks and estimate each three ways: optimistic, realistic, pessimistic. Name what's most likely to increase the time.
prompts.planning.estimate.refine: I only have [time]. What should I do first so there's at least some result?
prompts.planning.estimate.check: The task actually took [time]. Where was my estimate off?
prompts.planning.priorities.detailed: Here are my tasks: [task list]. Sort them into an urgent–important matrix as a table. For borderline ones, ask me a clarifying question instead of deciding for me. Finally suggest an order for the next 2 days and what can be postponed or dropped.
prompts.planning.priorities.refine: [task] matters to me even though it's not urgent. How can I make time for it?
prompts.planning.priorities.check: I've chosen this order: [order]. Is there a task here that actually blocks the others?
prompts.planning.checklist.detailed: Make a checklist for [task]. Split it into before, during and after. Each item is a concrete action that can be ticked off. Star the items people most often forget. No more than 15 items.
prompts.planning.checklist.refine: Make a short version with the 5 most important items.
prompts.planning.dependencies.detailed: Here are the project's tasks: [tasks]. Table: task, what must be done before it, what it unlocks, whether it can run in parallel. Below the table: the order of work and the chain of tasks where any delay would push back the whole project.
prompts.planning.dependencies.refine: [task] is delayed. What can be done in parallel while we wait?
prompts.planning.dependencies.check: I've set this order: [order]. Am I starting any task before what it needs is ready?
prompts.planning.project.detailed: Make a plan for the project “[project]”. People involved: [roles]. Deadline: [deadline]. Sections: goal and output, stages with dates, who's responsible for what (by role, no personal data), checkpoints, risks and what to do if they happen, how we'll track progress.
prompts.planning.project.refine: Add a short weekly status check: which 3 questions to ask the team.
prompts.planning.project.check: We're [time] behind plan. What are the options: cut scope, move the deadline, add people?
prompts.planning.review.short: Make a review plan for [topics] before [date].
prompts.planning.review.detailed: I need to review: [topics] before [date]. I can study [time] a day. Weak topics: [weak topics]. Make a plan with spaced repetition: when to learn, when to revisit, when to do a practice test. Give more time to weak topics. Keep the last day for light review only.
prompts.planning.review.refine: I've missed [days] days. How do I compress the plan without dropping review?
prompts.planning.review.check: Here are my practice test results: [results]. Which topics need another round?
prompts.planning.shortage.short: I'm running out of time. Help me rework the plan: [plan], [time] left.
prompts.planning.shortage.detailed: My plan was: [plan]. I have [time] left instead of the [time needed] I need. Help me rework it: what's essential for the result to count, what can be simplified, what can be cut. Suggest a new plan for the remaining time, with breaks for sleep and meals.
prompts.planning.shortage.refine: Help me write a short, polite message asking for an extension.
prompts.planning.shortage.check: What can I learn so I don't end up in this situation next time?
prompts.planning.rest.short: Help me balance my day between work and rest: [tasks]
prompts.planning.rest.detailed: Help me build a daily routine. Tasks: [tasks]. Fixed times: [schedule]. I usually get tired by [time]. Alternate work and rest, add short breaks, time to move, and time for things I enjoy: [hobbies]. Don't schedule work less than an hour before bed.
prompts.planning.rest.refine: Make a weekend version: fewer tasks, more free time.
prompts.planning.rest.check: I followed the routine for 3 days. Here's how it went: [how it went]. What should I change?

verify.planning.stages: The AI's plan doesn't know about your other commitments. Check you can actually spare that much time.
verify.planning.week: Don't fill the week to 100%: leave free slots for the unexpected and for rest.
verify.planning.estimate: Time estimates are almost always optimistic. Add 30–50% to the total.
verify.planning.priorities: You decide what's important. The AI only sees what you've written.
verify.planning.checklist: Walk through the checklist once for real and adjust it: missing steps show up in practice.
verify.planning.dependencies: Check the links yourself: the AI may treat tasks as independent when one actually needs another's output.
verify.planning.project: Agree the project plan with everyone involved: they may have their own constraints.
verify.planning.review: Review works better with gaps. Check the plan comes back to each topic after a few days.
verify.planning.shortage: If you're badly short on time, talk honestly with your teacher or manager about the deadline. That's a normal step.
verify.planning.rest: If tiredness doesn't go away after rest, that's a reason to talk to a doctor or someone close, not just to change your schedule.
